findings.title: Recovery-code creation uses wrong UserCredentialModel field
findings.body: In CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential the JSON of raw codes is passed via new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson), which populates getValue() (same pattern as createOTPCredential where storage reads getValue()). But BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential for recovery codes reads input.getChallengeResponse() to populate credentialData. Validation via UserCredentialModel.buildFromBackupAuthnCode uses challengeResponse, so creation and validation use different fields. Consequence is the federated provider receives null for credentialData, so recovery codes are not persisted correctly and subsequent login/validation fails or stores null.

findings.title: Federated recovery-code validation never consumes codes
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and never updates or removes the used code. Local recovery-code provider marks a code as used on successful isValid, and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator relies on that to eventually detect allCodesUsed. With this implementation the same recovery code remains valid forever, defeating one-time use, and allCodesUsed never becomes true. The added test only uses one code once, so reuse is never caught.

findings.title: getCredentials can NPE for unknown user
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials the code does var myUser = getMyUser(user) then immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without null check, unlike isValid and isConfiguredFor which check for null. If getCredentials is called for a user not in the map, myUser is null and this throws NullPointerException, breaking credential listing for federated users.

findings.title: Cannot disable/remove federated recovery codes
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType only clears myUser.otp for OTP types and logs otherwise, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream only advertises OTP. There is no handling for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE. As a result admin REST disableCredentialType, account-console delete, and any flow that disables recovery codes does nothing when codes live in user storage, leaving stale/exhausted credentials behind.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential removed via wrong API
findings.body: After successful validation the code looks up the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream, then calls removeStoredCredentialById with that ID when allCodesUsed. removeStoredCredentialById operates on local stored credentials, not federated credentials, and the test storage does not support disabling recovery codes. For a user whose codes live in user storage the exhausted credential is therefore never removed from the external store, so the user keeps an empty credential and the required-action logic diverges from local-storage behavior.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get causes 500 when credential missing
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean constructor does RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) then immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() without isPresent check, then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the user has no recovery credential or all codes are used, this throws NoSuchElementException during login-page rendering, producing a 500 instead of a handled error or redirect to setup.
